cycles.title: Cycle 1: Foundations
cycles.subtitle: Offensive Attacks → Blocking → Combinations → Live Application

overviewRows.fightIq: If you can touch, you can score

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon grip checks, guard transitions, Sprinter Stance / Samurai Guard mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Combat Zones 1-7 in order on wavemaster: Darkside strike, Lightside strike, Stab, Stab, Level Change (squat) dark, Level Change (squat) light, Rolex. Adjustment drill: slide as far as possible for distance using head gear to measure.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction Drill — instructor calls the zone, student strikes on command. Add Recovery (realign) after every rep.

cue.drillCue: "Call it, strike it, realign." No strike without a realign after.
cue.coachNote: Watch for students dropping weapon guard after the strike — realign is not optional.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does striking a specific zone in order (not randomly) matter before you ever spar?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: General movement + closed-stance zone bounce footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-4 on pads in order: Round Kick, Hook Kick, Punch, Side Kick. 30-second AMRAP through all zones. Adjustment: slide as far as possible (lunge punch) for distance.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction Drill — pad holder presents pads randomly at a consistent distance; student reacts and strikes whichever zone opens.

cue.drillCue: "Punch, crescent kick" — every single rep, no exceptions.
cue.coachNote: Recovery technique (punch, crescent kick) is the safety net — drill it as hard as the attack itself.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the difference between throwing a strike and running a play?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full-body movement prep, sparring + combat guard transitions.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run both Free Lunch versions back to back — Sparring Zones 1-4, then Combat Zones 1-7. Partner Reaction Drill in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 30-second AMRAP zone strikes (sparring) into 30-second AMRAP zone strikes (combat). Circular movement laps around the wavemaster/bag between sets.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Tetris Games: Sparring to 3 points, Combat to 5 points. Only Free Lunch zone strikes score.

cue.drillCue: "Score it clean, recover it clean." A play isn't finished until you've realigned.
cue.coachNote: This is the students' first live-scoring exposure this cycle — keep energy high, control contact.
cue.fightIqQ: In live rounds, which zone opened up the most for you, and why?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard flow + level-change mobility (knee, deep X-stance).

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-7: Line 8, Line 8, Level Change (knee) stab x2, Level Change (deep X-stance) light side x2, Guillotine. Move Development on Line 8 strikes. 20 Line 8 strikes for time.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Propellor Drill — swing belt in front of wavemaster, student strikes to hit pad before rope returns; random opening version.

cue.drillCue: "Beat the rope, not the clock." Timing over speed.
cue.coachNote: This play stacks two stab zones back to back — check that students aren't rushing the second stab.
cue.fightIqQ: What changes about your strategy when there's more than one way to score in the same play?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Zone bounce footwork, ankle/hip mobility for kicking zones.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-4: Axe Kick, Twist Kick, Round Kick, Front Kick. Move Development — Axe/Twist Kick Level 1 kill kicks. 30-second AMRAP.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Propellor Drill on wavemaster (swing belt/rope in front, student times a kick to beat it) — random opening version, then add Recovery (punch, evade).

cue.drillCue: "See the rope, read the zone, then strike." Reaction before technique.
cue.coachNote: Axe and Twist Kicks are higher Sparring I.Q. — slow the drill down before adding speed.
cue.fightIqQ: Why is a kick that's harder to throw sometimes easier to land?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Combined mobility flow — sparring + combat guard transitions.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run both Free Dessert versions. Propellor Drill with full Recovery added in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP with Recovery (both formats). Propellor Swinger moves around the bag to add ring movement.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Tetris Games: Sparring first to 3, Combat first to 5. Students may use Free Lunch OR Free Dessert zones to score.

cue.drillCue: "Two plays, one goal — score clean, recover clean."
cue.coachNote: First week letting students choose between two plays live — watch decision speed, not just execution.
cue.fightIqQ: When you had a choice of plays, what made you pick the one you picked?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Rooftop Guard entries from back stance, weapon control drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zone Blocks 1-7 from Rooftop Guard / Back Stance. Projectile Blocking (Marksman training remote) — partner attacks random zones.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Projectile Blocking with Recovery strike (Rooftop Drop — downward strike after the block).

cue.drillCue: "Block, then always answer." A block that doesn't lead somewhere is only half a play.
cue.coachNote: Rooftop Guard is a new stance for most students — isolate the stance before adding the block.
cue.fightIqQ: The manual says 'If you can touch, you can score, and if you can block, you can touch.' What does that mean for how you should think about blocking?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Guard-up footwork, hands-ready circular movement.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zone Blocks 1-4. Partner attacks random zones slowly but continuously — student blocks each.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill — hold a shield and combat weapon as a 'sword,' block opponent's random attacks continuously.

cue.drillCue: "If you can touch, you can score — so if you can block, you can touch."
cue.coachNote: This reframes blocking as offense-adjacent, not purely defensive — say it out loud in class.
cue.fightIqQ: How is a block secretly the first half of an attack?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Combined guard-up movement, sparring + combat.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Sparring Zone Blocks 1-4 and Combat Zone Blocks 1-7, partner attacking random zones continuously in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with no shield/sword (sparring); opponent walks toward you as you walk backward, Projectile Blocking with Recovery (combat).

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Guard Games: spar with different guard styles (Boxer, X-Guard, Cobra, Olympic-Straddled) in both sparring and combat — 'try on your opponent's armor.'

cue.drillCue: "You'll never know where the chinks are until you've worn the armor."
cue.coachNote: Rotate guard styles every 60-90 seconds so every student experiences at least 3 guards.
cue.fightIqQ: Which guard style felt hardest to attack against, and why?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard resets, alignment footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Zone Blocks 1-7 at full speed. Layer in Recovery — downward strike (Rooftop Drop) after every successful block, no pause.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Opponent walks toward you, you walk backward maintaining guard — Projectile Blocking with Recovery under constant closing pressure.

cue.drillCue: "Never a dead block." Every block ends in a strike.
cue.coachNote: Under closing pressure students collapse their guard — cue them to keep elbows in, base wide.
cue.fightIqQ: What happens to your options if you block but forget to recover?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Circular ring-ready movement, guard resets.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Zone Blocks 1-4 at full speed with continuous random attacks. Ring Ready — opponent attacks from random footwork and distancing while student maintains circular movement.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill continuous rounds — 3 x 45 seconds, 15 seconds rest.

cue.drillCue: "Stay round, stay ready." Circular movement never stops between blocks.
cue.coachNote: Watch for students squaring up and standing flat-footed after a block — reset their stance immediately.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does staying in motion after a block make you harder to hit next time?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Fast review of Zone Blocks (sparring 1-4 / combat 1-7) with Recovery attached to every rep.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill continuous rounds, both formats, 3 x 45 sec / 15 sec rest.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Guard Games live rounds — students spar and combat-spar switching guard styles every round on the coach's call. Score only counts off a block-into-recovery sequence.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.body: Quick partner share: one guard style you want to keep using.

cue.drillCue: "No free blocks." If you block it, you follow it.
cue.coachNote: This is the cycle's first fully live blocking round — praise recovery follow-through as much as the block itself.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one guard adjustment you're taking into next week's combos?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon flow drills, clockwise/counter-clockwise footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Clockwise or counter-clockwise combination striking down the line. Move Development — chaining Kill Kicks Level 1 & 2 on a partner.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP: down-and-back combination = 1 rep.

cue.drillCue: "You never know where the next zone opens — stay chained."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students stopping after the first strike lands — the combo isn't done until the chain is.
cue.fightIqQ: How does hitting one zone change which zone opens next?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Directional footwork — clockwise and counter-clockwise around the room.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: On Command: student hits a called zone AND the zone next to it, chaining the combination live.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner pad drill — increase opponent's distance, recover with a reverse side kick when they retreat out of range.

cue.drillCue: "Call it, chain it." Two zones, one continuous motion.
cue.coachNote: If a student's distance recovery kick is landing short, it's a distancing problem, not a technique problem.
cue.fightIqQ: What do you do differently when your opponent increases distance mid-combo?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Directional flow footwork, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Down-floor combination chains, both sparring and combat, mixing clockwise/counter-clockwise on command.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP combinations both formats; partner pad drill distance-recovery reps.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — combinations only score if two connected zones land in sequence. Single strikes don't count this round.

cue.drillCue: "One strike is an attack. Two connected strikes are a play."
cue.coachNote: This constraint (combos only) forces students to think in sequences — expect some frustration, that's the point.
cue.fightIqQ: What was harder tonight — landing the first strike or the second?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Aerial control prep — chamber and re-chamber drills for weapon in motion.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Repeated strike down the floor for distance/reps. Introduce TKD Running concept: once a checkpoint is established, maintain aerial control to chain into a follow-up strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: How far can you cover in 5/10/15 seconds with repeated strikes down the floor? Track and compare.

cue.drillCue: "Once you've got the checkpoint, the follow-up is free."
cue.coachNote: Aerial/weapon control after the first strike is the hard part — slow it down before racing the clock.
cue.fightIqQ: What does 'establishing a checkpoint' mean before you commit to the next strike?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Hop-kick chamber drills, hip mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Repeat Round Kick down the floor — how far can you hop-kick in 5/10/15 seconds. TKD Running: side kick to establish aerial control, chain into jump spin side/round/hook off a clap-count cue.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Golf scoring — recover with a punch if the foot hits the ground or the kick lands below the belt.

cue.drillCue: "Stay in your lane" — drag side kick spin chamber, switch chamber, no wasted motion.
cue.coachNote: This is the highest Sparring I.Q. content in the cycle — expect it to take reps. Praise attempts, not just clean landings.
cue.fightIqQ: Why is landing bouncing (not overextended) so important right after a long kick like this?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full aerial-control and chamber warm-up, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Lunch Box Method + Repeat Strikes + TKD Running — quick review reps in both sparring and combat.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Laps around the wavemaster/bag for time — students strike whichever zone their feet are facing on each pass.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — any Session 3 combination counts double if it lands as a full chain (2+ connected strikes).

cue.drillCue: "Chain it, don't rush it."
cue.coachNote: This closes out the combination block — note which 2-3 students are ready to be combo demo partners next cycle.
cue.fightIqQ: Of everything in this cycle so far — attack, block, combo — which do you trust most under pressure?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard + zone-strike flow, all three sessions.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice review reps — pick the weakest zone/block/combo observed this cycle and drill it.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec strikes / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Combat round robin — every play from Sessions 1-3 is live and scoring. No new material introduced.

cue.drillCue: "Everything's live now — attack, block, or chain, your choice."
cue.coachNote: Use this week to quietly assess who's ready for more complexity next cycle (Checking/Evading).
cue.fightIqQ: Which play did you reach for first tonight, and why that one?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full zone-strike and guard flow, all three sessions.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice review reps — target the weakest zone/block/combo observed this cycle.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec strikes / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Sparring round robin — every play from Sessions 1-3 is live and scoring.

cue.drillCue: "Read the zone before you commit."
cue.coachNote: This is a good week to rotate partners frequently — different body types expose different gaps.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one thing your partner did tonight that you want to try yourself?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full-body flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Instructor-led rapid review — one rep of each Session 1-3 play, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP both formats: 30 sec / 15 sec rest x 5 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Round Robin format — every student spars/combat-spars every partner in their row for 60 seconds, all cycle content live.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.body: Each student names one play they want to sharpen before Cycle 2.

cue.drillCue: "This is everything you've built this cycle — trust it."
cue.coachNote: Round Robin is high-energy; keep matches short and keep rotating so nobody stalls out.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the one play you most want to be automatic by the end of next cycle?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard flow.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark: AMRAP zone strikes in 90 seconds — record score, no rank comparison, just personal benchmark.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games, combat, first to 5 — all Session 1-3 plays legal.

cue.drillCue: "Play clean, play fast, recover every time."
cue.coachNote: Log each student's AMRAP number privately — useful for tracking progress cycle over cycle, not for testing.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the one habit from this cycle you don't want to lose over the next two months?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full zone-strike and guard flow.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark: AMRAP zone strikes in 90 seconds — record score, personal benchmark only.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games, sparring, first to 3 — all Session 1-3 plays legal.

cue.drillCue: "Play clean, play fast, recover every time."
cue.coachNote: Same benchmark structure as Combat Day — compare each student's own numbers, not against peers.
cue.fightIqQ: What would you do differently if you replayed tonight's games right now?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark both formats — 90-second AMRAP each. Personal tracking, not testing.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games tournament bracket — sparring first to 3, combat first to 5. Mix partners each round.

blocks.label: Cycle Reflection
blocks.body: Group discussion: name the 3 Concrete Elements covered this cycle (Attacking, Stopping) and preview Cycle 2 (Checking, Evading).

cue.drillCue: "No grading tonight — just show what two months built."
cue.coachNote: This is a celebration night, not an evaluation — keep the tone high-energy and low-pressure.
cue.fightIqQ: What are you most proud of from this cycle?

overviewRows.session: Home Base Games + Full Checking Review

overviewRows.fightIq: Win the exchange, not just survive it

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon grip and point-control drills, stance transitions for closing distance.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Paper Stabbing accuracy drill — stabbing has to land precisely since it can glance off the opponent. When opponent throws any strike on their way in, check them with a stab first.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Ring Ready — opponent attacks from random angles and distances; add circular movement between reps.

cue.drillCue: "Stab first, ask questions later — but only if it lands clean."
cue.coachNote: Accuracy over speed here — a glancing stab teaches bad habits. Slow the drill down before adding resistance.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does checking on the way in require better accuracy than checking after the attack has started?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Spin/chamber mobility, distance-awareness footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Three checking distances against a spin: Long distance = side kick, Mid distance = hip bump the spin and chamber, Short distance = punch. Partner bounces forward/backward to change distance, then randomly spins and chambers — student reads distance and checks with the correct tool.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction reps — follow every successful check with a strike or a realign, student's choice based on what opened.

cue.drillCue: "Read the range before you commit the check."
cue.coachNote: Most common mistake: using the same check regardless of distance. Call out the distance if a student defaults to one tool.
cue.fightIqQ: Why might checking a spinning opponent make them more unpredictable, not less?

days.playName: Off A Spin + Jousting — Full Review

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run Off A Spin (all 3 distances) in sparring, then Jousting accuracy reps in combat.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement laps with random-angle attacks, both formats — student must identify distance/angle and check correctly.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — checks only score if matched to the correct distance/situation. Coach calls out "good check" or "wrong tool" from the sideline.

cue.drillCue: "The right check at the wrong distance isn't a check — it's an opening."
cue.coachNote: This is the first time distance-matching is scored live — expect some hesitation as students think before reacting.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the risk of checking with the wrong tool for the distance?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Wrist mobility, cross-sticked vs. same-side-sticked guard recognition.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Two downward-strike checking options depending on guard match-up: Rolex (cross-sticked — hammer-fist-style downward strike from belly button through opponent's wrist and back) or Guillotine (same-side-sticked — downward strike from high guard, second half of a Fan Strike). Frying Pan pad holder extends with right or left hand; student reads and chooses Rolex or Guillotine.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Recovery — since these strikes finish downward at Zone 7, the natural follow-up is a High Level strike. Drill the recovery every rep.

cue.drillCue: "Read the stick, pick the strike." Cross-sticked = Rolex. Same-side = Guillotine.
cue.coachNote: This is a guard-recognition drill as much as a technique drill — slow it way down until the read is automatic.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does the SAME check not work against both cross-sticked and same-side-sticked opponents?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Invasion-distance footwork, jump-spin chamber mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: When a partner invades your space, check with a Side Kick. Side Kick Bag drill across the ring for time (scale kick level for younger/lighter students to avoid knocking the bag over).

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Recovery — Jump Evading Spin Hook after the check. Pad holder steps to extend the clapper pad so the student has a target for the evading jump spin kick.

cue.drillCue: "BRAAAAINS." — that's your cue the invasion is coming. Check, then evade-spin away.
cue.coachNote: This play chains a check directly into an evasive counter — don't let students stop after the side kick.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does a Jump Evading Spin Hook make sense as the recovery right after checking an invading opponent?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Quick review of all four Checking plays: Off A Spin, Jousting, Rolex Check, Zombie Slayer.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec check-and-recover reps / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds, both formats.

blocks.label: Live Application — Zombie Slayer Game
blocks.body: One "Slayer" stands in the center of the ring; multiple "Zombies" (holding shield + clapper pad) close in announcing "BRAAAINS." Slayer checks with a Side Kick and recovers with an Evading Jump Spin Hook. Rotate the Slayer every 60-90 seconds. Run Home Base Games for combat.

cue.drillCue: "You can't check what you don't see coming — stay circular, stay aware."
cue.coachNote: This is a high-energy, favorite-format night — use it to build buy-in before the denser Evading block starts next week.
cue.fightIqQ: Which of the four Checking plays felt most natural to you, and which needs the most work?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard flow, wrist and stance mobility.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice — drill whichever of Jousting or Rolex Check needs the most work based on Week 10 observation. Layer in random guard match-ups (cross-sticked / same-side-sticked) for Rolex Check.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with random-angle attacks, checking on command.

cue.drillCue: "No wasted checks — every one earns a recovery."
cue.coachNote: This is a targeted-remediation day — use your Week 10 notes to pick what each group actually needs.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one checking mistake you caught yourself making last week, and how did you fix it?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Distance-reading footwork, spin/chamber mobility.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice — drill whichever of Off A Spin (3 distances) or Zombie Slayer needs the most work. Mix in random invasion + spin attacks so students must identify which checking play applies.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction reps — instructor calls out an attack type, student picks and executes the correct check.

cue.drillCue: "Name the attack, pick the check."
cue.coachNote: By now students should be choosing between checking plays, not just executing one on cue — test that judgment.
cue.fightIqQ: How do you decide which checking play to use when you don't know what's coming?

days.playName: Home Base Games — Full Checking Live

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Rapid-fire review — one rep of each of the four Checking plays, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP both formats: 30 sec / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Application — Home Base Games
blocks.body: Home Base Games, sparring and combat — all four Checking plays are live and scoring. Students choose their check based on what's actually presented.

cue.drillCue: "This is everything Checking has taught you — trust the read."
cue.coachNote: This closes the Checking block — note which students are ready for the more reactive Evading content next week.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the difference between checking on reflex and checking on a read?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard mobility, lateral head/shoulder movement drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Evading has two methods: Backwards (Arrow Method) and Forward (Slipping). Since you can't go straight to 12:00 (that's invading), slip to 10 or 2 o'clock — whichever side is opposite the strike coming in.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner throws a strike; student evades to the opposite side they're being struck on. Add Recovery — since slipping brings you closer to your opponent, follow with a strike.

cue.drillCue: "Go where the strike isn't — 10 or 2, never 12."
cue.coachNote: Slipping forward is counterintuitive for students used to retreating — reassure them proximity is the point.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does slipping forward put you in a better position than backing straight away?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Head-movement and footwork mobility, closed-stance flow.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slip to 11 or 1 o'clock — go to the opposite side you're being struck on. Never slip straight to 12:00, that's invading directly into the opponent.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner strikes with a variety of techniques mixed with random footwork; student evades to the opposite side. Add Recovery — follow the slip with a strike since you're now inside striking range.

cue.drillCue: "11 or 1 — pick a side and commit."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students freezing mid-slip — a half-committed slip is worse than no slip at all.
cue.fightIqQ: Mr. Miyagi said 'best block, not be there' — how does slipping put that idea into practice?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run Slipping in both formats — Sparring (11 & 1) then Combat (10 & 2) — with Recovery strike added every rep.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with random footwork and distancing, both formats, evading on command.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — points only count if they come immediately after a successful slip. Straight retreats don't score.

cue.drillCue: "Slip first, strike second — every time."
cue.coachNote: Students will want to just back away under pressure — this constraint forces the forward evade they need to practice.
cue.fightIqQ: What did slipping forward feel like the first few times versus by the end of class?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard mobility with added circular footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slipping (10 & 2) against random footwork and distancing — opponent no longer telegraphs. Layer in Ring Ready circular movement between exchanges so evading becomes continuous, not just reactive to one strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Slip-and-strike combination reps for time — track how many clean slip-to-strike sequences in 60 seconds.

cue.drillCue: "Never stop moving after the slip — stay circular."
cue.coachNote: This week raises unpredictability — expect more missed slips than Week 12. That's the point of the progression.
cue.fightIqQ: What's harder — slipping one predictable strike, or slipping in a live, moving exchange?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Circular ring-ready footwork, reaction-speed drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slipping (11 & 1) against random footwork and distancing. Add Ring Ready circular movement so students are already moving before the strike comes, not standing flat-footed waiting to react.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Slip-and-strike combination reps for time — track clean sequences in 60 seconds.

cue.drillCue: "Moving targets are hard to hit — stay circular before AND after the slip."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students who slip correctly but then plant their feet and stop moving — that's the next habit to fix.
cue.fightIqQ: How does staying in motion before the strike even comes change how easy the slip is?

blocks.label: Warm-Up

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Use the 3 R's Strategy (RZM, Read, React). RZM: throw Lightside painting/pointing/pump fakes to get a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and what they open when they stop your set-up. React: Lightside strike to the opening. Drag for distance, strike, then step back farther after every landed strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pointing RZM sequence: Samurai Guard, extend arm at 80% speed until opponent anchors their front foot, then read and Lightside strike low.

cue.drillCue: "The fake isn't the point — the opponent's reaction is the point."

blocks.label: Drill

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner holds a clapper pad; as you go to kick it, they try to smack your foot with the pad. When you see them reaching, pull the kick and punch their other pad.

cue.drillCue: "See the smack coming? Pull it, and make them pay with the punch."
cue.coachNote: This is a reading drill disguised as a kicking drill — praise the read, not just the pull.
cue.fightIqQ: How is a Fake different from just faking someone out by accident?

blocks.label: Live Application

cue.drillCue: "No reaction, no fake — just a strike."

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Samurai Guard entries, weapon-grab efficiency drills (empty hand to weapon transition).

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: RZM: throw an empty-hand strike to draw a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and what they open. React: grab your weapon and Lightside strike the opening. Alternate empty-hand strike at the bag, grab weapon, strike bag — build efficiency for 30 seconds.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Fight Illiteracy / Learn to Read drill: opponent commits to the same response every time you throw the RZM so students can practice reading the pattern before it's randomized.

cue.drillCue: "Empty hand first, weapon second — never fumble the grab."
cue.coachNote: The weapon-grab transition is the technical bottleneck here — isolate it before adding the fake's timing.
cue.fightIqQ: Why might attacking empty-handed first make your weapon strike more likely to land?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Pivot mobility, kick-chamber transitions.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: RZM: throw a Front Kick or Side Kick to draw a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and Stopping style. React: pivot aggressively to free your leg from the block and throw a Round Kick — the shape of the motion looks like a zig-zag.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pad drill: get as close to the bag as possible with the kick before pivoting, which launches the round kick into the bag.

cue.drillCue: "Get blocked on purpose — then pivot away from it."
cue.coachNote: Students often pivot too early, before the block actually lands — the fake only works if the first kick looks committed.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does the first kick need to look like a real attack for this fake to work?

blocks.body: Telephone Fake: set up with the weapon in Telephone position to mess with the opponent's timing and distancing, then strike wherever opens. Vince Carter: from High Guard, initiate a Number 1 or Number 8 Line RZM, then lift your back leg to hand the weapon off between your legs, land, and strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pad drill: weapon in Telephone position, let go, re-grab, strike the bag — repeat for 30 seconds to build a clean, unmissed re-grab.

cue.drillCue: "Mess with their timing before you ever commit to the strike."

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Drag Reverse Side Kick the bag for distance; when you touch, switch to a Round Kick. For Axe Kick: drag for distance, then switch when the pad exposes.

cue.drillCue: "Commit to the side kick, then surprise them with the switch."
cue.coachNote: This is the highest-coordination Fake in the sparring set — expect it to take the most reps of anything this cycle.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Countering uses the 3 R's like a Fake, but the RZM is Defensive instead of Offensive. RZM: bait the opponent into attacking by exposing your radial nerve. Read: identify their Reaction Zone and what they open when they take the bait. React: evade while handing the weapon off between your legs, land, and strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning

cue.drillCue: "Bait the attack, don't wait for it."

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: This is a Stop WITH Attack — the counter is a block and a score in one motion. Spin Hook Kick with a high chamber and as little telegraphing as possible. RZM: bait your partner into kicking toward you, drawing them in as deep as possible. Read: identify their Reaction Zone and what Attack they used. React: spin hook kick through the opening.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: "Hot Potato" pad drill — both partners hold a clapper pad and alternate spin hook kicking each other's pads. Stop on the instructor's call; last person to kick owes a squat.

cue.drillCue: "Draw them in deep — the deeper the bait, the cleaner the counter."
cue.coachNote: Telegraphing is the main leak here — cue students to keep the chamber high and tight before the kick fires.

blocks.label: Conditioning

blocks.label: Drill

React: check with a Side Kick, plant outside their leg, then throw the Hawkeye.

blocks.label: Conditioning

cue.drillCue: "Check first, position second, Hawkeye last."

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon grip checks, guard transitions, Sprinter Stance / Samurai Guard mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Combat Zones 1-7 in order on wavemaster: Darkside strike, Lightside strike, Stab, Stab, Level Change (squat) dark, Level Change (squat) light, Rolex. Adjustment drill: slide as far as possible for distance using head gear to measure.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction Drill — instructor calls the zone, student strikes on command. Add Recovery (realign) after every rep.

cue.drillCue: "Call it, strike it, realign." No strike without a realign after.
cue.coachNote: Watch for students dropping weapon guard after the strike — realign is not optional.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does striking a specific zone in order (not randomly) matter before you ever spar?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: General movement + closed-stance zone bounce footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-4 on pads in order: Round Kick, Hook Kick, Punch, Side Kick. 30-second AMRAP through all zones. Adjustment: slide as far as possible (lunge punch) for distance.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction Drill — pad holder presents pads randomly at a consistent distance; student reacts and strikes whichever zone opens.

cue.drillCue: "Punch, crescent kick" — every single rep, no exceptions.
cue.coachNote: Recovery technique (punch, crescent kick) is the safety net — drill it as hard as the attack itself.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the difference between throwing a strike and running a play?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full-body movement prep, sparring + combat guard transitions.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run both Free Lunch versions back to back — Sparring Zones 1-4, then Combat Zones 1-7. Partner Reaction Drill in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 30-second AMRAP zone strikes (sparring) into 30-second AMRAP zone strikes (combat). Circular movement laps around the wavemaster/bag between sets.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Tetris Games: Sparring to 3 points, Combat to 5 points. Only Free Lunch zone strikes score.

cue.drillCue: "Score it clean, recover it clean." A play isn't finished until you've realigned.
cue.coachNote: This is the students' first live-scoring exposure this cycle — keep energy high, control contact.
cue.fightIqQ: In live rounds, which zone opened up the most for you, and why?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard flow + level-change mobility (knee, deep X-stance).

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-7: Line 8, Line 8, Level Change (knee) stab x2, Level Change (deep X-stance) light side x2, Guillotine. Move Development on Line 8 strikes. 20 Line 8 strikes for time.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Propellor Drill — swing belt in front of wavemaster, student strikes to hit pad before rope returns; random opening version.

cue.drillCue: "Beat the rope, not the clock." Timing over speed.
cue.coachNote: This play stacks two stab zones back to back — check that students aren't rushing the second stab.
cue.fightIqQ: What changes about your strategy when there's more than one way to score in the same play?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Zone bounce footwork, ankle/hip mobility for kicking zones.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zones 1-4: Axe Kick, Twist Kick, Round Kick, Front Kick. Move Development — Axe/Twist Kick Level 1 kill kicks. 30-second AMRAP.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Propellor Drill on wavemaster (swing belt/rope in front, student times a kick to beat it) — random opening version, then add Recovery (punch, evade).

cue.drillCue: "See the rope, read the zone, then strike." Reaction before technique.
cue.coachNote: Axe and Twist Kicks are higher Sparring I.Q. — slow the drill down before adding speed.
cue.fightIqQ: Why is a kick that's harder to throw sometimes easier to land?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Combined mobility flow — sparring + combat guard transitions.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run both Free Dessert versions. Propellor Drill with full Recovery added in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP with Recovery (both formats). Propellor Swinger moves around the bag to add ring movement.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Tetris Games: Sparring first to 3, Combat first to 5. Students may use Free Lunch OR Free Dessert zones to score.

cue.drillCue: "Two plays, one goal — score clean, recover clean."
cue.coachNote: First week letting students choose between two plays live — watch decision speed, not just execution.
cue.fightIqQ: When you had a choice of plays, what made you pick the one you picked?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Rooftop Guard entries from back stance, weapon control drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zone Blocks 1-7 from Rooftop Guard / Back Stance. Projectile Blocking (Marksman training remote) — partner attacks random zones.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Projectile Blocking with Recovery strike (Rooftop Drop — downward strike after the block).

cue.drillCue: "Block, then always answer." A block that doesn't lead somewhere is only half a play.
cue.coachNote: Rooftop Guard is a new stance for most students — isolate the stance before adding the block.
cue.fightIqQ: The manual says 'If you can touch, you can score, and if you can block, you can touch.' What does that mean for how you should think about blocking?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Guard-up footwork, hands-ready circular movement.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Memorize Zone Blocks 1-4. Partner attacks random zones slowly but continuously — student blocks each.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill — hold a shield and combat weapon as a 'sword,' block opponent's random attacks continuously.

cue.drillCue: "If you can touch, you can score — so if you can block, you can touch."
cue.coachNote: This reframes blocking as offense-adjacent, not purely defensive — say it out loud in class.
cue.fightIqQ: How is a block secretly the first half of an attack?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Combined guard-up movement, sparring + combat.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Sparring Zone Blocks 1-4 and Combat Zone Blocks 1-7, partner attacking random zones continuously in both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with no shield/sword (sparring); opponent walks toward you as you walk backward, Projectile Blocking with Recovery (combat).

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Guard Games: spar with different guard styles (Boxer, X-Guard, Cobra, Olympic-Straddled) in both sparring and combat — 'try on your opponent's armor.'

cue.drillCue: "You'll never know where the chinks are until you've worn the armor."
cue.coachNote: Rotate guard styles every 60-90 seconds so every student experiences at least 3 guards.
cue.fightIqQ: Which guard style felt hardest to attack against, and why?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard resets, alignment footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Zone Blocks 1-7 at full speed. Layer in Recovery — downward strike (Rooftop Drop) after every successful block, no pause.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Opponent walks toward you, you walk backward maintaining guard — Projectile Blocking with Recovery under constant closing pressure.

cue.drillCue: "Never a dead block." Every block ends in a strike.
cue.coachNote: Under closing pressure students collapse their guard — cue them to keep elbows in, base wide.
cue.fightIqQ: What happens to your options if you block but forget to recover?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Circular ring-ready movement, guard resets.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Zone Blocks 1-4 at full speed with continuous random attacks. Ring Ready — opponent attacks from random footwork and distancing while student maintains circular movement.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill continuous rounds — 3 x 45 seconds, 15 seconds rest.

cue.drillCue: "Stay round, stay ready." Circular movement never stops between blocks.
cue.coachNote: Watch for students squaring up and standing flat-footed after a block — reset their stance immediately.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does staying in motion after a block make you harder to hit next time?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Fast review of Zone Blocks (sparring 1-4 / combat 1-7) with Recovery attached to every rep.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Spartan Drill continuous rounds, both formats, 3 x 45 sec / 15 sec rest.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Guard Games live rounds — students spar and combat-spar switching guard styles every round on the coach's call. Score only counts off a block-into-recovery sequence.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.body: Quick partner share: one guard style you want to keep using.

cue.drillCue: "No free blocks." If you block it, you follow it.
cue.coachNote: This is the cycle's first fully live blocking round — praise recovery follow-through as much as the block itself.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one guard adjustment you're taking into next week's combos?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon flow drills, clockwise/counter-clockwise footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Clockwise or counter-clockwise combination striking down the line. Move Development — chaining Kill Kicks Level 1 & 2 on a partner.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP: down-and-back combination = 1 rep.

cue.drillCue: "You never know where the next zone opens — stay chained."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students stopping after the first strike lands — the combo isn't done until the chain is.
cue.fightIqQ: How does hitting one zone change which zone opens next?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Directional footwork — clockwise and counter-clockwise around the room.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: On Command: student hits a called zone AND the zone next to it, chaining the combination live.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner pad drill — increase opponent's distance, recover with a reverse side kick when they retreat out of range.

cue.drillCue: "Call it, chain it." Two zones, one continuous motion.
cue.coachNote: If a student's distance recovery kick is landing short, it's a distancing problem, not a technique problem.
cue.fightIqQ: What do you do differently when your opponent increases distance mid-combo?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Directional flow footwork, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Down-floor combination chains, both sparring and combat, mixing clockwise/counter-clockwise on command.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: 60-second AMRAP combinations both formats; partner pad drill distance-recovery reps.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — combinations only score if two connected zones land in sequence. Single strikes don't count this round.

cue.drillCue: "One strike is an attack. Two connected strikes are a play."
cue.coachNote: This constraint (combos only) forces students to think in sequences — expect some frustration, that's the point.
cue.fightIqQ: What was harder tonight — landing the first strike or the second?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Aerial control prep — chamber and re-chamber drills for weapon in motion.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Repeated strike down the floor for distance/reps. Introduce TKD Running concept: once a checkpoint is established, maintain aerial control to chain into a follow-up strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: How far can you cover in 5/10/15 seconds with repeated strikes down the floor? Track and compare.

cue.drillCue: "Once you've got the checkpoint, the follow-up is free."
cue.coachNote: Aerial/weapon control after the first strike is the hard part — slow it down before racing the clock.
cue.fightIqQ: What does 'establishing a checkpoint' mean before you commit to the next strike?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Hop-kick chamber drills, hip mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Repeat Round Kick down the floor — how far can you hop-kick in 5/10/15 seconds. TKD Running: side kick to establish aerial control, chain into jump spin side/round/hook off a clap-count cue.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Golf scoring — recover with a punch if the foot hits the ground or the kick lands below the belt.

cue.drillCue: "Stay in your lane" — drag side kick spin chamber, switch chamber, no wasted motion.
cue.coachNote: This is the highest Sparring I.Q. content in the cycle — expect it to take reps. Praise attempts, not just clean landings.
cue.fightIqQ: Why is landing bouncing (not overextended) so important right after a long kick like this?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full aerial-control and chamber warm-up, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Lunch Box Method + Repeat Strikes + TKD Running — quick review reps in both sparring and combat.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Laps around the wavemaster/bag for time — students strike whichever zone their feet are facing on each pass.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — any Session 3 combination counts double if it lands as a full chain (2+ connected strikes).

cue.drillCue: "Chain it, don't rush it."
cue.coachNote: This closes out the combination block — note which 2-3 students are ready to be combo demo partners next cycle.
cue.fightIqQ: Of everything in this cycle so far — attack, block, combo — which do you trust most under pressure?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard + zone-strike flow, all three sessions.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice review reps — pick the weakest zone/block/combo observed this cycle and drill it.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec strikes / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Combat round robin — every play from Sessions 1-3 is live and scoring. No new material introduced.

cue.drillCue: "Everything's live now — attack, block, or chain, your choice."
cue.coachNote: Use this week to quietly assess who's ready for more complexity next cycle (Checking/Evading).
cue.fightIqQ: Which play did you reach for first tonight, and why that one?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full zone-strike and guard flow, all three sessions.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice review reps — target the weakest zone/block/combo observed this cycle.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec strikes / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Sparring round robin — every play from Sessions 1-3 is live and scoring.

cue.drillCue: "Read the zone before you commit."
cue.coachNote: This is a good week to rotate partners frequently — different body types expose different gaps.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one thing your partner did tonight that you want to try yourself?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full-body flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Instructor-led rapid review — one rep of each Session 1-3 play, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP both formats: 30 sec / 15 sec rest x 5 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Rounds
blocks.body: Round Robin format — every student spars/combat-spars every partner in their row for 60 seconds, all cycle content live.

blocks.label: Reflection
blocks.body: Each student names one play they want to sharpen before Cycle 2.

cue.drillCue: "This is everything you've built this cycle — trust it."
cue.coachNote: Round Robin is high-energy; keep matches short and keep rotating so nobody stalls out.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the one play you most want to be automatic by the end of next cycle?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard flow.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark: AMRAP zone strikes in 90 seconds — record score, no rank comparison, just personal benchmark.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games, combat, first to 5 — all Session 1-3 plays legal.

cue.drillCue: "Play clean, play fast, recover every time."
cue.coachNote: Log each student's AMRAP number privately — useful for tracking progress cycle over cycle, not for testing.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the one habit from this cycle you don't want to lose over the next two months?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full zone-strike and guard flow.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark: AMRAP zone strikes in 90 seconds — record score, personal benchmark only.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games, sparring, first to 3 — all Session 1-3 plays legal.

cue.drillCue: "Play clean, play fast, recover every time."
cue.coachNote: Same benchmark structure as Combat Day — compare each student's own numbers, not against peers.
cue.fightIqQ: What would you do differently if you replayed tonight's games right now?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning Peak
blocks.body: For-time benchmark both formats — 90-second AMRAP each. Personal tracking, not testing.

blocks.label: Games
blocks.body: Tetris Games tournament bracket — sparring first to 3, combat first to 5. Mix partners each round.

blocks.label: Cycle Reflection
blocks.body: Group discussion: name the 3 Concrete Elements covered this cycle (Attacking, Stopping) and preview Cycle 2 (Checking, Evading).

cue.drillCue: "No grading tonight — just show what two months built."
cue.coachNote: This is a celebration night, not an evaluation — keep the tone high-energy and low-pressure.
cue.fightIqQ: What are you most proud of from this cycle?

overviewRows.session: Home Base Games + Full Checking Review

overviewRows.fightIq: Win the exchange, not just survive it

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon grip and point-control drills, stance transitions for closing distance.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Paper Stabbing accuracy drill — stabbing has to land precisely since it can glance off the opponent. When opponent throws any strike on their way in, check them with a stab first.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Ring Ready — opponent attacks from random angles and distances; add circular movement between reps.

cue.drillCue: "Stab first, ask questions later — but only if it lands clean."
cue.coachNote: Accuracy over speed here — a glancing stab teaches bad habits. Slow the drill down before adding resistance.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does checking on the way in require better accuracy than checking after the attack has started?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Spin/chamber mobility, distance-awareness footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Three checking distances against a spin: Long distance = side kick, Mid distance = hip bump the spin and chamber, Short distance = punch. Partner bounces forward/backward to change distance, then randomly spins and chambers — student reads distance and checks with the correct tool.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction reps — follow every successful check with a strike or a realign, student's choice based on what opened.

cue.drillCue: "Read the range before you commit the check."
cue.coachNote: Most common mistake: using the same check regardless of distance. Call out the distance if a student defaults to one tool.
cue.fightIqQ: Why might checking a spinning opponent make them more unpredictable, not less?

days.playName: Off A Spin + Jousting — Full Review

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run Off A Spin (all 3 distances) in sparring, then Jousting accuracy reps in combat.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement laps with random-angle attacks, both formats — student must identify distance/angle and check correctly.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — checks only score if matched to the correct distance/situation. Coach calls out "good check" or "wrong tool" from the sideline.

cue.drillCue: "The right check at the wrong distance isn't a check — it's an opening."
cue.coachNote: This is the first time distance-matching is scored live — expect some hesitation as students think before reacting.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the risk of checking with the wrong tool for the distance?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Wrist mobility, cross-sticked vs. same-side-sticked guard recognition.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Two downward-strike checking options depending on guard match-up: Rolex (cross-sticked — hammer-fist-style downward strike from belly button through opponent's wrist and back) or Guillotine (same-side-sticked — downward strike from high guard, second half of a Fan Strike). Frying Pan pad holder extends with right or left hand; student reads and chooses Rolex or Guillotine.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Recovery — since these strikes finish downward at Zone 7, the natural follow-up is a High Level strike. Drill the recovery every rep.

cue.drillCue: "Read the stick, pick the strike." Cross-sticked = Rolex. Same-side = Guillotine.
cue.coachNote: This is a guard-recognition drill as much as a technique drill — slow it way down until the read is automatic.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does the SAME check not work against both cross-sticked and same-side-sticked opponents?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Invasion-distance footwork, jump-spin chamber mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: When a partner invades your space, check with a Side Kick. Side Kick Bag drill across the ring for time (scale kick level for younger/lighter students to avoid knocking the bag over).

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Recovery — Jump Evading Spin Hook after the check. Pad holder steps to extend the clapper pad so the student has a target for the evading jump spin kick.

cue.drillCue: "BRAAAAINS." — that's your cue the invasion is coming. Check, then evade-spin away.
cue.coachNote: This play chains a check directly into an evasive counter — don't let students stop after the side kick.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does a Jump Evading Spin Hook make sense as the recovery right after checking an invading opponent?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Quick review of all four Checking plays: Off A Spin, Jousting, Rolex Check, Zombie Slayer.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec check-and-recover reps / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds, both formats.

blocks.label: Live Application — Zombie Slayer Game
blocks.body: One "Slayer" stands in the center of the ring; multiple "Zombies" (holding shield + clapper pad) close in announcing "BRAAAINS." Slayer checks with a Side Kick and recovers with an Evading Jump Spin Hook. Rotate the Slayer every 60-90 seconds. Run Home Base Games for combat.

cue.drillCue: "You can't check what you don't see coming — stay circular, stay aware."
cue.coachNote: This is a high-energy, favorite-format night — use it to build buy-in before the denser Evading block starts next week.
cue.fightIqQ: Which of the four Checking plays felt most natural to you, and which needs the most work?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard flow, wrist and stance mobility.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice — drill whichever of Jousting or Rolex Check needs the most work based on Week 10 observation. Layer in random guard match-ups (cross-sticked / same-side-sticked) for Rolex Check.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with random-angle attacks, checking on command.

cue.drillCue: "No wasted checks — every one earns a recovery."
cue.coachNote: This is a targeted-remediation day — use your Week 10 notes to pick what each group actually needs.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one checking mistake you caught yourself making last week, and how did you fix it?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Distance-reading footwork, spin/chamber mobility.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Coach's choice — drill whichever of Off A Spin (3 distances) or Zombie Slayer needs the most work. Mix in random invasion + spin attacks so students must identify which checking play applies.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction reps — instructor calls out an attack type, student picks and executes the correct check.

cue.drillCue: "Name the attack, pick the check."
cue.coachNote: By now students should be choosing between checking plays, not just executing one on cue — test that judgment.
cue.fightIqQ: How do you decide which checking play to use when you don't know what's coming?

days.playName: Home Base Games — Full Checking Live

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Rapid-fire review — one rep of each of the four Checking plays, both formats.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP both formats: 30 sec / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Live Application — Home Base Games
blocks.body: Home Base Games, sparring and combat — all four Checking plays are live and scoring. Students choose their check based on what's actually presented.

cue.drillCue: "This is everything Checking has taught you — trust the read."
cue.coachNote: This closes the Checking block — note which students are ready for the more reactive Evading content next week.
cue.fightIqQ: What's the difference between checking on reflex and checking on a read?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard mobility, lateral head/shoulder movement drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Evading has two methods: Backwards (Arrow Method) and Forward (Slipping). Since you can't go straight to 12:00 (that's invading), slip to 10 or 2 o'clock — whichever side is opposite the strike coming in.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner throws a strike; student evades to the opposite side they're being struck on. Add Recovery — since slipping brings you closer to your opponent, follow with a strike.

cue.drillCue: "Go where the strike isn't — 10 or 2, never 12."
cue.coachNote: Slipping forward is counterintuitive for students used to retreating — reassure them proximity is the point.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does slipping forward put you in a better position than backing straight away?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Head-movement and footwork mobility, closed-stance flow.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slip to 11 or 1 o'clock — go to the opposite side you're being struck on. Never slip straight to 12:00, that's invading directly into the opponent.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner strikes with a variety of techniques mixed with random footwork; student evades to the opposite side. Add Recovery — follow the slip with a strike since you're now inside striking range.

cue.drillCue: "11 or 1 — pick a side and commit."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students freezing mid-slip — a half-committed slip is worse than no slip at all.
cue.fightIqQ: Mr. Miyagi said 'best block, not be there' — how does slipping put that idea into practice?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Run Slipping in both formats — Sparring (11 & 1) then Combat (10 & 2) — with Recovery strike added every rep.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Circular movement with random footwork and distancing, both formats, evading on command.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — points only count if they come immediately after a successful slip. Straight retreats don't score.

cue.drillCue: "Slip first, strike second — every time."
cue.coachNote: Students will want to just back away under pressure — this constraint forces the forward evade they need to practice.
cue.fightIqQ: What did slipping forward feel like the first few times versus by the end of class?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Weapon guard mobility with added circular footwork.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slipping (10 & 2) against random footwork and distancing — opponent no longer telegraphs. Layer in Ring Ready circular movement between exchanges so evading becomes continuous, not just reactive to one strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Slip-and-strike combination reps for time — track how many clean slip-to-strike sequences in 60 seconds.

cue.drillCue: "Never stop moving after the slip — stay circular."
cue.coachNote: This week raises unpredictability — expect more missed slips than Week 12. That's the point of the progression.
cue.fightIqQ: What's harder — slipping one predictable strike, or slipping in a live, moving exchange?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Circular ring-ready footwork, reaction-speed drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Slipping (11 & 1) against random footwork and distancing. Add Ring Ready circular movement so students are already moving before the strike comes, not standing flat-footed waiting to react.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Slip-and-strike combination reps for time — track clean sequences in 60 seconds.

cue.drillCue: "Moving targets are hard to hit — stay circular before AND after the slip."
cue.coachNote: Watch for students who slip correctly but then plant their feet and stop moving — that's the next habit to fix.
cue.fightIqQ: How does staying in motion before the strike even comes change how easy the slip is?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review
blocks.body: Ring Ready circular movement into random-attack slipping, both formats, with Recovery strike required every rep.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Slip-and-strike combination AMRAP, both formats — 60 seconds each, track personal counts.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — evading and checking are both legal; students choose which Stopping tool fits what's presented.

cue.drillCue: "Check it or slip it — but never just eat it."
cue.coachNote: This is the first week students choose freely between Checking (Weeks 9-11) and Evading (Weeks 12-13) live — watch decision-making, not just execution.
cue.fightIqQ: When you had a choice between checking and slipping, what made you pick the one you picked?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full weapon guard and slip mobility flow.

blocks.label: Skill Review
blocks.body: Fast review of Slipping (10 & 2) with Recovery, plus a refresher on the four Checking plays.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Interval AMRAP: 30 sec slip-and-strike / 15 sec rest x 4 rounds.

blocks.label: Games — Sudden Victory Battles
blocks.body: First scoring exchange wins the round. Any Session 4 or 5 play may be used to set up or seal the win.

cue.drillCue: "Sudden victory — the first clean exchange ends it."

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Use the 3 R's Strategy (RZM, Read, React). RZM: throw Lightside painting/pointing/pump fakes to get a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and what they open when they stop your set-up. React: Lightside strike to the opening. Drag for distance, strike, then step back farther after every landed strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pointing RZM sequence: Samurai Guard, extend arm at 80% speed until opponent anchors their front foot, then read and Lightside strike low.

cue.drillCue: "The fake isn't the point — the opponent's reaction is the point."
cue.coachNote: This is the first Mental Profile content this program — slow way down on the Read step before adding speed.

blocks.label: Warm-Up

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Use the 3 R's Strategy (RZM, Read, React). RZM: throw offensive set-ups to draw a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and Stopping style. React: pull your kick back and land the best punch to score — punch should land before your foot returns to the ground.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner holds a clapper pad; as you go to kick it, they try to smack your foot with the pad. When you see them reaching, pull the kick and punch their other pad.

cue.drillCue: "See the smack coming? Pull it, and make them pay with the punch."
cue.coachNote: This is a reading drill disguised as a kicking drill — praise the read, not just the pull.
cue.fightIqQ: How is a Fake different from just faking someone out by accident?

days.playName: Lightside Fakes + Pull 'N' Punch — Full Review

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Full mobility flow, both formats.

blocks.label: Drill Review

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Reaction Zone pad drills, both formats — partner provides the stopping mechanism, student reads and reacts live.

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — a fake only counts as "successful" (coach call-out) if it draws a real reaction before the scoring strike lands.

cue.drillCue: "No reaction, no fake — just a strike."
cue.coachNote: This is students' first live exposure to the Mental Profile — expect them to default back to Natural Profile (just striking) under pressure. That's normal at this stage.
cue.fightIqQ: What's one moment tonight you baited a real reaction out of your partner?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Samurai Guard entries, weapon-grab efficiency drills (empty hand to weapon transition).

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: RZM: throw an empty-hand strike to draw a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and what they open. React: grab your weapon and Lightside strike the opening. Alternate empty-hand strike at the bag, grab weapon, strike bag — build efficiency for 30 seconds.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Fight Illiteracy / Learn to Read drill: opponent commits to the same response every time you throw the RZM so students can practice reading the pattern before it's randomized.

cue.drillCue: "Empty hand first, weapon second — never fumble the grab."
cue.coachNote: The weapon-grab transition is the technical bottleneck here — isolate it before adding the fake's timing.
cue.fightIqQ: Why might attacking empty-handed first make your weapon strike more likely to land?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Pivot mobility, kick-chamber transitions.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: RZM: throw a Front Kick or Side Kick to draw a reaction. Read: identify the opponent's Reaction Zone and Stopping style. React: pivot aggressively to free your leg from the block and throw a Round Kick — the shape of the motion looks like a zig-zag.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pad drill: get as close to the bag as possible with the kick before pivoting, which launches the round kick into the bag.

cue.drillCue: "Get blocked on purpose — then pivot away from it."
cue.coachNote: Students often pivot too early, before the block actually lands — the fake only works if the first kick looks committed.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does the first kick need to look like a real attack for this fake to work?

blocks.label: Warm-Up

blocks.label: Live Application

cue.drillCue: "Two more tools in the bag — same rule: bait, read, react."

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Telephone-position weapon carry, weapon hand-off mobility (between the legs).

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Telephone Fake: set up with the weapon in Telephone position to mess with the opponent's timing and distancing, then strike wherever opens. Vince Carter: from High Guard, initiate a Number 1 or Number 8 Line RZM, then lift your back leg to hand the weapon off between your legs, land, and strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pad drill: weapon in Telephone position, let go, re-grab, strike the bag — repeat for 30 seconds to build a clean, unmissed re-grab.

cue.drillCue: "Mess with their timing before you ever commit to the strike."
cue.coachNote: Vince Carter's hand-off is a coordination challenge — expect drops early on, that's part of learning it.
cue.fightIqQ: How does simply changing your weapon position (without attacking) already put your opponent at a disadvantage?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Side kick aerial-control chamber drills, jump-switch mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Side Kick for aerial control, jump and switch into Round Kick, Axe Kick, or Front Kick. Pad drill: chamber the back leg in side kick position on the bag; on the partner's "Go" call, jump and switch kick.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Drag Reverse Side Kick the bag for distance; when you touch, switch to a Round Kick. For Axe Kick: drag for distance, then switch when the pad exposes.

cue.drillCue: "Commit to the side kick, then surprise them with the switch."
cue.coachNote: This is the highest-coordination Fake in the sparring set — expect it to take the most reps of anything this cycle.
cue.fightIqQ: What makes a fake with a jump and switch harder to defend than a fake on the ground?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Radial-nerve awareness drills, weapon hand-off mobility.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Countering uses the 3 R's like a Fake, but the RZM is Defensive instead of Offensive. RZM: bait the opponent into attacking by exposing your radial nerve. Read: identify their Reaction Zone and what they open when they take the bait. React: evade while handing the weapon off between your legs, land, and strike.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Pointing RZM: begin in High Guard, throw a Dark Side or downward strike RZM at 80% speed waiting for opponent to defend, then read and react.

cue.drillCue: "Bait the attack, don't wait for it."
cue.coachNote: This is students' first exposure to a Defensive RZM — contrast it with last cycle's Offensive RZM fakes so the distinction is clear.
cue.fightIqQ: How is baiting an attack (Countering) different from baiting a block (Faking)?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Spin/chamber mobility with a focus on minimizing telegraph.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: This is a Stop WITH Attack — the counter is a block and a score in one motion. Spin Hook Kick with a high chamber and as little telegraphing as possible. RZM: bait your partner into kicking toward you, drawing them in as deep as possible. Read: identify their Reaction Zone and what Attack they used. React: spin hook kick through the opening.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: "Hot Potato" pad drill — both partners hold a clapper pad and alternate spin hook kicking each other's pads. Stop on the instructor's call; last person to kick owes a squat.

cue.drillCue: "Draw them in deep — the deeper the bait, the cleaner the counter."
cue.coachNote: Telegraphing is the main leak here — cue students to keep the chamber high and tight before the kick fires.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does baiting your opponent to attack you first sometimes beat attacking first yourself?

days.playName: Vince Carter + Blocking Spin Hook Kick — Full Review

blocks.label: Warm-Up

blocks.label: Drill Review

blocks.label: Conditioning

blocks.label: Live Application
blocks.body: Live rounds — a counter only counts (coach call-out) if it's built off a real bait, not just a lucky read.

cue.drillCue: "Bait it, read it, counter it — in that order, every time."
cue.coachNote: This is the first live Countering exposure — expect students to counter opportunistically at first rather than intentionally baiting. Coach the bait step specifically.

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Disengaging-jump mobility, front-leg evade drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: This is a Stop THEN Attack — front leg evades, leading into a disengaging jump. As you ascend, the weapon comes down in a Number 8 Line Strike simultaneously. Depending on opponent placement, a Dark Side or Light Side strike may be available on the way down.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Partner pad drill — down the floor, strike the opponent with random strikes for them to practice Golden Roostering to different targets. Follow every rep with a strike or realign.

cue.drillCue: "Evade up, strike on the way down."
cue.coachNote: The timing window here is tight — the strike must land during the ascending jump, not after. Slow it down before adding resistance.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does evading upward (instead of backward) create a scoring opportunity here?

blocks.label: Warm-Up
blocks.body: Hip-rotation mobility, outside-leg positioning drills.

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: Rotate your kicking leg, hip, and shoulder toward your opponent while standing outside their leg, hip to hip. Bend over as you rotate and kick your leg up like a scorpion tail into the back of their head. RZM: bait them into kicking toward you, drawing them in deep. Read: identify their Reaction Zone. React: check with a Side Kick, plant outside their leg, then throw the Hawkeye.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Hawkeye pad drill — partner holds a shield and stomps at you; check with a Side Kick, land outside the opponent's leg, and Hawkeye Counter.

cue.drillCue: "Check first, position second, Hawkeye last."
cue.coachNote: This counter has three distinct steps in sequence — break it into pieces before chaining it live.
cue.fightIqQ: Why does landing outside your opponent's leg (not in front of them) set up this counter?

blocks.label: Drill
blocks.body: An Attack WITH a Stop built in. As you spin hook kick (or spin Hawkeye), bury your head to your knee like an ostrich in the sand, and throw your back leg up into a kick. RZM: bait them into kicking toward you, drawing them in deep. Read: identify their Reaction Zone. React: as they kick at your head, dive your head down and throw your back leg into a hook kick or Hawkeye.

blocks.label: Conditioning
blocks.body: Tie a kinetic band across two wavemasters; duck under and hook or Hawkeye over the band to build the head-dive habit safely.

cue.drillCue: "Head down, leg up — the dive IS the block."
cue.coachNote: This is the most defensively literal counter in the cycle — students must trust the head-dive fully or they'll get caught halfway.
